one_line: Last great Sena king and his two successors holding on in eastern Bengal after the fall of Nabadwip.

appearance.age_look: Lakshmanasena appears as a dignified man in his late 60s, Vishvarupasena as a determined prince in his late 20s, and Keshavasena as a calm ruler in his mid-30s, all lean and athletic rather than bulky.
appearance.face: All three share a gently angular Bengali face with straight nose, medium-brown complexion and sharp anime eyes; Lakshmanasena has fine forehead lines and a trimmed grey moustache-beard with a thoughtful, slightly melancholic default expression, Vishvarupasena’s expression is intense and watchful with a light moustache and no beard, and Keshavasena’s expression is composed and resolute with a neatly trimmed full moustache and short beard.
appearance.hair: Lakshmanasena has long, mostly grey-black hair tied into a high, smooth topknot at the crown with the rest coiled into a compact bun, held by a thin gold circlet; Vishvarupasena’s black hair is pulled into a tighter topknot with a small knot of hair and a plain dark cloth band; Keshavasena’s dark hair is similarly tied but shorter at the back, bound with a simple gold headband engraved with a tiny central lotus.
appearance.costume: They all wear late-12th–13th-century eastern Indian royal attire: layered cotton-silk garments with wrapped lower cloths and tailored sashes. Lakshmanasena’s main outfit is a rich deep-maroon silk uttariya (upper cloth) draped over both shoulders and crossing his chest over a long-sleeved, light-cream cotton tunic that reaches mid-thigh, paired with a ankle-length off-white dhoti tightly wrapped and pleated in front with a thin maroon border, and a wide woven gold-and-red waist-belt; he wears minimal but fine jewellery—medium-width gold armlets, a single gold torque-necklace with a small central pendant, simple round gold earrings, and a few thin bangles—plus narrow leather sandals. Vishvarupasena’s design emphasizes a warrior-prince in the retreat east: he wears a fitted short-sleeved dark indigo cotton tunic with subtle vertical weave texture, over which sits a sleeveless quilted cotton armour vest (brigandine style) in muted brown with stitched rectangular panels, tied with side cords; his lower garment is a pale-ochre dhoti wrapped to just above the ankle with a indigo border, secured by a broad red cloth sash knotted at his left hip with flowing ends, and he carries a simple cloth shoulder-bag at his back, with light sandals laced around the ankles. Keshavasena, embodying restored dignity in Vikrampura, wears a more courtly but practical ensemble: a fine pale-green long tunic with narrow sleeves and knee-length hem, decorated with a subtle woven floral pattern at the cuffs and hem, over which a soft saffron-gold sash crosses diagonally from shoulder to waist; his dhoti is light-cream with a double border in green and gold, and he has a slightly narrower gold waist-belt; his jewellery is modest—small drop-shaped gold earrings and one slim armlet on his right arm—indicating reduced but present royal resources, with simple brown leather sandals.
appearance.signature: A single elaborately hilted pata-style straight sword, era-appropriate to eastern India with a long slightly tapering blade and a rigid gauntlet-like grip, housed in a plain dark-brown scabbard with minimal brass fittings, is the shared prop: Lakshmanasena uses it as a ceremonial symbol resting by his side, Vishvarupasena wears it slung by a strap across his back ready for sudden movement, and Keshavasena keeps it sheathed at his left hip as a sign of continuing authority rather than constant battle.

ref_desc: Three related Bengali Sena rulers share similar angular faces and topknotted hair: Lakshmanasena in maroon silk over cream tunic and off-white dhoti, Vishvarupasena in indigo tunic with quilted brown vest and ochre dhoti, and Keshavasena in pale-green long tunic with cream dhoti, all accompanied by a single shared dark-sheathed pata sword and a palette of maroon, indigo, cream, muted gold and pale green.
sheet_prompt: Draw three full-body anime-style Bengali Sena rulers from c.1200–1250 CE as a consistent trio: Lakshmanasena as an elder king in deep-maroon silk uttariya over a light-cream long tunic and off-white ankle-length dhoti with maroon border, wearing a thin gold circlet on his grey-black topknot, modest gold armlets, torque and earrings, standing with a dignified, thoughtful expression beside a dark-brown sheathed pata sword with minimal brass fittings; Vishvarupasena as a late-20s warrior-prince with black hair in a tight topknot and a cloth headband, intense watchful eyes, a fitted dark indigo short-sleeved tunic covered by a sleeveless brown quilted cotton armour vest, pale-ochre dhoti to the ankles with indigo border, broad red hip sash, simple shoulder-bag and light sandals, the same pata sword slung on his back; and Keshavasena in his mid-30s, composed and resolute, with dark hair tied back and a simple gold lotus headband, wearing a pale-green patterned knee-length long-sleeved tunic with subtle floral borders, saffron-gold diagonal sash, light-cream dhoti with green-and-gold border and narrow gold waist-belt, small gold earrings and a single armlet, the shared sword sheathed at his left hip; show them together on a neutral background, emphasizing consistent facial structure, shared family resemblance, tied topknot hairstyles, historically grounded 13th-century eastern Indian textiles and jewellery, and the dominant colours maroon, indigo, cream, muted gold and pale green.
